strategies.name: Baseline Eight Sequential All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Directly implements the reference with 8 dependent all_reduce operations, each preceded by local scale-by-a[r] and followed by local scale-by-1/a[r]. Expected 8 all_reduce dispatches plus local element-wise ops. Represents the straightforward approach with maximum dispatch overhead but simplest logic.

strategies.name: Fused Local Ops Between Collectives
strategies.desc: Merges the scale/divide operations and buffer cloning into single fused kernels between each all_reduce, reducing memory traffic and kernel launch overhead. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but fewer local-op dispatches (8 fused kernels instead of ~24 separate scale/clone/divide ops). Trades kernel complexity for reduced dispatch count on local operations.

strategies.name: Vectorized Scaling with Precomputed Coefficients
strategies.desc: Precomputes all scaling coefficients (a[r], 1/a[r], a[r]/W) into tensors and uses batched element-wise multiplications instead of per-shard loops. 8 all_reduce dispatches remain, but local ops become vectorized broadcasts/multiplies. Reduces Python loop overhead and enables better memory access patterns at cost of additional temporary buffers.

strategies.name: Two-Phase Reduce-Scatter All-Gather Chain
strategies.desc: Replaces each all_reduce with a reduce_scatter followed by all_gather to pipeline communication with computation. After reduce_scatter, only 1/W of data per rank; apply scaling there, then all_gather. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG) but smaller intermediate payloads and opportunity to overlap computation during scatter phase. Trades collective count for reduced per-collective bandwidth.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Tree Reduction
strategies.desc:
Exploits potential multi-node topology by structuring the 8 iterations as intra-node all_reduce followed by inter-node all_reduce, with scaling applied at node-granularity intermediate results. Requires 16 collectives (8 intra-node + 8 inter-node) but leverages faster intra-node links for bulk of traffic. Only beneficial at multi-node scale; trades dispatch count for bandwidth hierarchy exploitation.
